s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and pelvic mass with chronic unilateral lower limb edema
salient_findings: Right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
Firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant
Multiple uterine fibroids
Large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
key_facts: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg
Regular menses
No tobacco or alcohol use
Afebrile, blood pressure 110/80 mmHg, pulse 88 beats/min
Respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Normal cardiac and respiratory examinations
Normal neurologic exam
Firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
Right adnexal mass confirmed by bimanual pelvic examination
Normal baseline hematologic, biochemical, thyroid, renal, and HIV/HBV/HCV serologies
Tumor markers within reference range
Pap smear was negative
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion

differentials: Solitary fibrous tumor of the ovary
per_call: Solitary fibrous tumor of the ovary

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Concerning imaging findings for an ovarian neoplasm and presence of a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and imaging characteristics to ovarian cystadenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common type of ovarian cancer and possible explanation for the patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Ovarian fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the patient's pelvic mass and chronic unilateral lower limb edema

shortlist.label: Krukenberg tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible diagnosis to consider given the patient's presentation and imaging findings

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large, solid-cystic lesion in the right adnexa, as seen on transvaginal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT, is concerning for an ovarian neoplasm. The imaging findings, along with the patient's symptoms of right lower abdominal pain, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ovarian fibroma
rejected.why: Ovarian fibroma typically presents as a solid, benign tumor, which does not match the solid-cystic lesion seen in this patient's imaging studies.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While mucinous cystadenocarcinoma is a type of ovarian cancer, the imaging findings do not specifically suggest a mucinous subtype.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to mucinous cystadenocarcinoma, serous cystadenocarcinoma is a type of ovarian cancer, but the imaging findings do not specifically suggest a serous subtype.

rejected.label: Krukenberg tumor
rejected.why: Krukenberg tumor typically presents with bilateral ovarian involvement and a known primary malignancy, which is not the case in this patient.
